- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods; reduce forecast peaks when sentiment is positive or neutral.
- Underestimate prices after strong negative sentiment spikes; adjust downward bias when sentiment turns negative.
- Lagging forecasts tend to overreact to recent price drops; smooth out delayed rebounds in forecasted price paths.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., sentiment spike → price surge) should be capped or moderated to avoid overcorrection.
- Mean-reversion bias is present in forecasts that ignore recent volatility; align forecasts with recent 7–14 day moving averages.
- When sentiment is consistently low or negative, reduce forecast volatility and avoid sharp upward revisions.
- Forecast errors are more pronounced in early horizon (1–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; apply more conservative adjustments for short-term predictions.
- If sentiment is trending upward but price is flat or declining, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.
- Avoid forecasting price spikes when sentiment is weak or mixed; prioritize stability over momentum in low-sentiment periods.
